Springwood High School celebrates best-ever Ofsted report
Springwood High School in King’s Lynn is celebrating its highest-ever rating following a two-day Ofsted inspection on October 20 and 21. Inspectors praised the school’s positive culture, stable leadership, and excellent pastoral support, describing the environment as feeling like a family. The report highlighted the school’s robust curriculum and a wide range of extra-curricular activities, noting that pupils feel safe and supported.
While the school was commended for its vibrant community spirit, inspectors suggested that leaders should continue to refine strategies for pupils facing multiple barriers to learning. Executive head teacher Andrew Johnson expressed his pride in the staff and students, describing the outcome as a reflection of their daily dedication.

Wisbech veteran honoured with National Service medal
A 93-year-old Wisbech veteran has been presented with a medal to honour his National Service following the Second World War. Gordon Phoenix, a former member of the medical corps, received the award during a surprise ceremony held at the town’s new veterans hub on Wednesday.
The medal was funded by local shop workers and community members who organised the presentation to recognise Mr Phoenix’s service. The event was hosted by the Wisbech branch of the Royal British Legion and attended by the veteran’s friends and family. Mr Phoenix is a well-known figure in the local community and an honorary member of the town’s football club.

item.title: Medical records accessed unlawfully at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Medical records accessed unlawfully at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
New figures reveal that staff at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn accessed medical records without authorisation on 107 occasions between 2021 and 2026. Hospital management stated that while most incidents involved employees viewing their own files, one case concerned a patient’s records. That specific matter was investigated and reported to the Information Commissioner’s Office.
The hospital’s director of people and culture, Zoe Baxter, emphasised that staff are regularly reminded that accessing records for personal reasons is unlawful. Across the country, over 3,000 similar incidents were recorded by NHS staff during the same five-year period. The East of England Ambulance Service Trust reported 182 cases of inappropriate access within that timeframe.

Christmas Golden Age fair returns to Wisbech for over 60s
Fenland District Council is hosting its Christmas Golden Age fair for residents aged over 60. The free event takes place at the Hudson Leisure Centre in Wisbech on Friday, December 11, between 10am and 1pm. Visitors can enjoy refreshments, entertainment, and access advice on topics including transport, finances, and wellbeing. Attendees will also receive a Christmas gift, provided through a partnership with the How Are You Fenland? project.
The council is still accepting donations of new, unwrapped gifts at local libraries and supermarkets until December 4. The fair is open to older residents, as well as their carers, family members, and advocates. Further details on the event and gift donation points are available via the Fenland District Council website.

West Norfolk Council approves land sale for new ambulance hub
West Norfolk Council has agreed to sell three and a half acres of land at Morston Drift in South Lynn to the East of England Ambulance Service. The site is set to be transformed into a new ambulance base serving the local area and beyond.
The land, which was previously considered for housing and business use, has been identified by the NHS Trust as an ideal location for its operations. The council plans to proceed with the sale once the ambulance service secures the necessary planning permission. While the authority confirmed it will receive a capital receipt from the transaction, the specific financial details have not been disclosed.

item.title: Terrington St Clement man cleared of assault charges
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Terrington St Clement man cleared of assault charges
A 22-year-old man from Terrington St Clement has been cleared of assault and stalking charges at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Ryley Dale, of Waterloo Road, had faced allegations including intentional strangulation, criminal damage, and harassment of an ex-partner between 2023 and 2024. During a summary trial on Wednesday, November 11, the Crown Prosecution Service offered no evidence, leading to the charges being dropped.
Mr. Dale previously gained public attention in September 2024 for his actions during a house fire in Gaywood. He was credited with helping to save four people from the property on Lynn Road after forcing entry to the building.
